layers.note: A tree of dry bluffs, rocky slopes and the edges of Douglas-fir forest near salt water.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 900 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Intermediate shade tolerance: leans out toward light.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about 0 °C, gone by −4 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −15 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −22 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 14 to 26 °C; gone below 12 °C, where summers are too short, and above 30 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long warm season: about 3,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,600 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,100: it stays in warm lowlands and on the lower slopes.

moisture_index.note: Summer drought borne: a moisture index from about 0.32 (gone by 0.2), dry savanna and prairie climates included.

summer_rain.note: A Mediterranean-type climate: its range lies where at most about 0.2 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.35.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Pacific madrone grows near the coast from south-west British Columbia to southern California, frost-tender and on dry summer slopes (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
